en: To present (an argument or a plea), especially in a legal case.
To beg, beseech, or implore, especially emotionally.

plead.ety: From Middle English pleden, plaiden, from Old French plaider (“to plead, offer a plea”), from plait, from Medieval Latin placitum (“a decree, sentence, suit, plea, etc.", in Classical Latin, "an opinion, determination, prescription, order; literally, that which is pleasing, pleasure”), neuter of placitus, past participle of placeō (“to please”). Cognate with Spanish pleitear (“to litigate, take to court”).

ex.en: Tom pleaded to his mother for money.
ex.ja: トムはお母さんにお金をねだった。

ex.en: The criminal pleaded with him to change his mind.
ex.ja: 罪人は考えを変えるよう彼に懇願した。

ex.en: Tom pleaded with his mother for money.
ex.ja: トムはお母さんにお金をねだった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 plaidier（訴える）から。plea と同じ。「嘆願する・申し立てる」。

en: To defecate.
To defecate in or on something.
Fecal matter; feces.
An act of defecation.
Expressing annoyed disappointment.

poop.ety: Uncertain, possibly from Middle English poupen (“to make a gulping sound while drinking, blow on a horn, toot”). Compare Dutch poepen (“to defecate”), German Low German pupen (“to fart; break wind”). Also representing poo pronounced with the mouth snapped closed at the end.

ex.en: I do not want to clean up dog poop.
ex.ja: 俺は犬のフンなんてかたづけたくない。

ex.en: Mom, I have to poop.
ex.ja: ママ、うんちしたい。

ex.en: My car is covered with pigeon poop.
ex.ja: 俺の車、鳩のフンまみれだよ。

en: The explicit literary or visual depiction of sexual subject matter; any display of material of an erotic nature.
The depiction of (non-sexual) subject matter so that it elicits feelings analogous to erotic pleasure; any such depiction.
To turn into pornography.

pornography.ety: Borrowed from French pornographie. By surface analysis, porno- + -graphy.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pornē（娼婦）+ graphein（書く）。graph と同じ。

en: The quality or condition of being prevalent; wide extension or spread.
The total number of cases of a disease in a given statistical population at a given time, divided by the number of individuals in that po…

note.ja: prevalent（広まっている）+ -ence。pre（前に・上に）+ valere（強い）。「優勢であること」→「普及・蔓延」。

en: To declare formally, officially or ceremoniously.
To declare authoritatively, or as a formal expert opinion.
Eggcorn of pronouns.

pronounce.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *per-der.?
Proto-Indo-European *per-der.?
Proto-Indo-European *pér
Proto-Indo-European *-o
Proto-Indo-European *pró
Proto-Indo-European *pro-
Proto-Italic *pro-
Latin prō-
Latin nūntius

Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂

Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂yéti

Proto-Italic *-āō

Middle English pronouncen
English pronounce

ex.en: Is there anyone who can pronounce this word?
ex.ja: 誰かこの単語を発音できる人はいますか。

ex.en: I'm not sure how to pronounce this word.
ex.ja: この単語の発音に確信はないです。

ex.en: We've been pronouncing it wrong the entire time.
ex.ja: 今まで発音を間違えてたよ。

note.ja: pro（前に）+ nounc（告げる）+ e。人前で告げる →「発音する・宣言する」。pronunciation（発音）は綴りが変わる点に注意。

en: Temporary, but with the intention of eventually becoming permanent or being replaced by a permanent equivalent.
A postage stamp issued locally before an official issue is released.
An interim denture.

provisional.ety: From provision + -al, or else from Middle French provisionnal (modern French provisionnel). Compare Latin prōvīsiōnālis.

ex.en: We'll have our firm's attorneys look through the provisional agreement.
ex.ja: 社の弁護士に暫定合意の内容を吟味してもらおう。

note.ja: provision（備え）+ -al。pro（前もって）+ videre（見る）。「前もって備えた」→「暫定的な」。provide と同じ vid。

en: Synonym of pay back in all senses.
To make worthwhile; to yield a result worth the effort; to pay off.

repay.ety: From Old French repaier (“to pay back”), from re- + paiier (“to pay”), from Latin pācāre (“to settle, to make peaceful”), from pāx (“peace”) + -ō (forming verbs). Equivalent to re- + pay. Cognate with repacify and French repayer (“to pay again”).

ex.en: I think that he repaid the money.
ex.ja: 彼はお金を返したと思う。

ex.en: He promised to repay the money, but I doubt his word.
ex.ja: 彼はお金を返してくれると約束したが疑わしいと思う。

ex.en: I must repay the debt.
ex.ja: 借金を返さなければならない。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ pay（払う）。「返済する・報いる」。

en: Of a reddish pink colour.
Red or pink makeup to add colour to the cheeks; blusher.
Any reddish pink colour.
To apply rouge (makeup).

rouge.ety: Borrowed from French rouge, from Latin rubeus. Compare rare Middle English rouge, rouȝ (“red”); later borrowed again, as it is not attested until c. 1750. The game senses are of unknown origin according to the Oxford English Dictionary.

ex.en: Expressions and smiles change like that just from applying rouge and lipstick.
ex.ja: ほお紅や口紅を差すだけで表情や笑顔がどんどん変わってくるんです。

note.ja: フランス語 rouge（赤）から。ラテン語 rubeus。ruby と同じ。「頬紅」。

en: UK, Canada, New Zealand, Australia, and Ireland spelling of rumor.
Commonwealth standard spelling of rumor.

rumour.ety: From Middle English rumour, from Old French rumour, rumor, from Latin rūmor (“common talk”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *rewH- (“to shout, roar”).

ex.en: That rumour is not true, is it?
ex.ja: そのうわさは本当ではないでしょうね。

ex.en: Who did you hear that rumour from?
ex.ja: その噂、誰から聞いたの？

ex.en: From whom did you hear that rumour?
ex.ja: その噂、誰から聞いたの？

note.ja: rumor のイギリスのつづり。

en: Full; unable to hold or contain any more.
Soaked or drenched with moisture.
A saturated hydrocarbon.

ex.en: He saturated himself with sunshine.
ex.ja: 彼は日光を全身に浴びた。

note.ja: saturate（飽和させる）+ -ed。ラテン語 satur（満腹の）。「いっぱいに満たされた」→「飽和した」。satisfy と同じ sat。

en: Drenched with water, or other liquid.

ex.en: Tom was completely soaked by the rain.
ex.ja: トムは雨で全身びしょぬれになった。

ex.en: Tom got soaked and caught a cold.
ex.ja: トムはずぶ濡れになって、風邪をひいた。

ex.en: We were soaked to the skin but very happy.
ex.ja: 私たちはずぶぬれになっていたが、とっても幸せだった。

note.ja: soak（浸す）+ -ed。soak は suck（吸う）と同系。「びしょぬれの」。

en: A game similar to baseball but played with a larger and softer ball which can be thrown overhand or underhand.
The ball used to play the sport.

ex.en: Do you know how to play softball?
ex.ja: ソフトボールのやり方、知ってる？

note.ja: soft（柔らかい）+ ball。「ソフトボール」。

en: Of or pertaining to the southeast.

southeastern.ety: From Middle English *southesterne, from Old English sūþēasterne, equivalent to south + eastern.

ex.en: Croatia is in the southeastern part of Europe.
ex.ja: クロアチアはヨーロッパの東南部に位置する国である。

ex.en: Croatia is located in the southeastern part of Europe.
ex.ja: クロアチアはヨーロッパの東南部に位置する国である。

ex.en: Croatia is a country in southeastern Europe.
ex.ja: クロアチアはヨーロッパの東南部に位置する国である。

note.ja: south（南）+ east（東）+ -ern。「南東の」。

en: One who watches an event; especially, an event held outdoors.
One who observes, sees, or views something; an observer.

spectator.ety: Borrowed from Latin spectātor, from frequentative verb spectō (“watch”), from speciō (“look at”). Equivalent to spectate + -or. Doublet of speculator.

ex.en: The spectators were excited by his home run.
ex.ja: 彼のホームランは観衆を沸かせた。

ex.en: There were more spectators than I had expected.
ex.ja: 予想以上に多くの観客が来ていました。

ex.en: The judge bound the spectators to keep quiet.
ex.ja: 判事は傍聴人に静かにするよう警告した。

note.ja: spect（見る）+ ator（人）。見る人 →「観客・見物人」。

en: The act and skills of presenting stories and tales.
A fall, trip or substantial misstep.
An error or blunder.
To misstep; to walk or run clumsily; to trip or fall.
To make mistakes, to have trouble.

stumble.ety: Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *stam- (“to trip up; to stammer, stutter”), thereby related to German stumm (“mute”), Dutch stom (“dumb”). Doublet of stammer. Also related to verb in Dutch stommelen (“to walk silently”).

ex.en: Why do I always stumble through life like this?
ex.ja: どうして僕はこんな不器用な生き方しかできないんだろう。

ex.en: She walked carefully so as not to stumble over a rock.
ex.ja: 石につまづかないように彼女は注意深く歩を進めた。

ex.en: The kid stumbled and fell to his knees.
ex.ja: その子供は、つまずいて転んで膝を突いた。

note.ja: 北欧語に由来するとされる。「つまずく」→ つまずいて見つける →「偶然出くわす（stumble upon）」。

en: The property of being stupid.
An act that is stupid.

stupidity.ety: From Latin stupiditātem, accusative of Latin stupiditās, equivalent to stupid + -ity.

ex.en: Thanks to your stupidity, we lost the game.
ex.ja: 君が間抜けだったおかげで、僕たちはその試合に負けたんだ。

ex.en: Everyone is responsible for his own stupidity.
ex.ja: 誰もが自分自身の愚かさに責任がある。

ex.en: I wish you'd quit that sort of super-league stupidity.
ex.ja: そういう度を越したアホはやめて欲しいですねー。

note.ja: stupid（愚かな）+ -ity。ラテン語 stupere（呆然とする）。「愚かさ」。stupor（意識もうろう）と同じ。

en: To put an end to, especially with force, to crush, do away with; to prohibit, subdue.
To restrain or repress, such as laughter or an expression.

suppress.ety: From Latin suppressus, perfect passive participle of supprimō (“press down or under”), from sub (“under”) + premō (“press”).

ex.en: I wonder how I can suppress this feeling.
ex.ja: どうすれば、この気持を抑えられるのだろう。

ex.en: The government tried to suppress all opposition parties.
ex.ja: 政府はすべての野党を抑圧しようとした。

ex.en: The news was suppressed for the time being.
ex.ja: そのニュースは当分の間差し止めになった。

note.ja: sup（下へ）+ press（押す）。押さえつける →「鎮圧する・抑える」。

en: Touchable; able to be touched or felt; perceptible by the sense of touch.
Perceptible; able to be perceived.
A physical object; something that can be touched.
Real or concrete results.

tangible.ety: Borrowed from Middle French tangible, from Late Latin tangibilis, from Latin tangere (“to touch”)

ex.en: Show me tangible data.
ex.ja: 具体的なデータを示しなさい。

ex.en: Service economy is a useful labor that does not produce a tangible commodity.
ex.ja: サービス経済は物を生産しないが有益な労働である。

en: To slope or incline (something); to slant.
To be at an angle.
A slope or inclination.
The inclination of part of the body, such as backbone, pelvis, head, etc.

tilt.ety:
From Middle English tilte, from Old English *tyltan, *tieltan (“to be unsteady”), related to the adjective tealt (“unsteady”), from Proto-West Germanic *talt, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *del-, *dul- (“to shake, hesitate”), see also Dutch touteren (“to tremble”), North Frisian talt, tolt (“unstable, shaky”). Cognate with Icelandic tölt (“an ambling pace”).
The nominal sense of "a joust" appears around 1510, presumably derived from the barrier which separated the combatants, which suggests connection with tilt "covering". The modern transitive meaning is from 1590; the intransitive use

ex.en: The pillar tilted to the right and fell.
ex.ja: 柱は右へ傾いて倒れた。

ex.en: She stood silently, her head tilted slightly to one side.
ex.ja: 彼女はちょっと首をかしげて、黙然と立っていた。

ex.en: I tilt my head. Not the pawn, but the knight?
ex.ja: 僕は首をひねる。このポーンではなくて、こっちのナイトを・・・。

note.ja: 古英語 tealt（不安定な）から。「傾ける」。

en: Ignorable; of little significance or value.
Commonplace, ordinary.

trivial.ety:
PIE word
 *tréyes
* From Latin triviālis (“appropriate to the street-corner, commonplace, vulgar”), from trivium (“place where three roads meet”). Compare trivium, trivia.
* From the distinction between trivium (“the lower division of the liberal arts; grammar, logic and rhetoric”) and quadrivium (“the higher division of the seven liberal arts in the Middle Ages, composed of geometry, astronomy, arithmetic, and music”).

ex.en: He easily gets angry at trivial things.
ex.ja: 彼はつまらないことですぐ怒る。

ex.en: Don't worry about such a trivial problem.
ex.ja: そんなささいな問題にくよくよするなよ。

ex.en: Women talk about trivial things when talking with men.
ex.ja: 女性が男性と話すとき、彼女たちはどうでもいいことを話す。

note.ja: ラテン語 trivium（三叉路）から。tri（3）+ via（道）。「三叉路の井戸端会議の話」→「ささいな」。via と同じ。

en: A member of any of the various ethnic groups that speak the Turkic languages.
A member of a West Asian ethnic group native to Anatolia (which comprises the bulk of their modern nation-state of Türkiye).
Synonym of Turkic.
Synonym of Turkish.

Turk.ety: From Middle English Turke, Turk, from Old French Turc, from Medieval Latin Turcus, from Medieval Greek Τοῦρκος (Toûrkos), from Classical Persian تُرْک (turk), from Middle Persian [script needed] (twlk' /⁠turk⁠/), from Old Turkic 𐱅𐰇𐰼𐰜 (t²ẅr²ẅk²). See Proto-Turkic *tür(ü)k for more.

ex.en: No, I'm not a German, I'm a Turk.
ex.ja: いいえ。ドイツ人じゃなくて、トルコ人です。

ex.en: Constantinople fell to the hands of the Ottoman Turks in 1453.
ex.ja: 1453年、コンスタンティノープルはオスマン帝国の手に渡った。

ex.en: Cockburn Town is the capital of the Turks and Caicos Islands.
ex.ja: コックバーンタウンは、タークス・カイコス諸島の首都です。

note.ja: トルコ人。Turkey（トルコ）と同じ。

en: Not officially established.
Implicitly true but withheld and/or contradicted by authority.

unofficial.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Germanic *un-
Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-
Middle English un-
English un-
English official
English unofficial
From un- + official.

note.ja: un（否定）+ official（公式の）。「非公式の」。

en: Something hung up or spread out to hide or protect the face, or hide an object from view; usually of gauze, crepe, or similar diaphanous …
Anything that partially obscures a clear view.
To dress in, or decorate with, a veil.
To conceal as with a veil.

veil.ety: From Middle English veil, veyl, from Anglo-Norman and Old Northern French veil (“sail, veil, shroud”) (Francien Old French voil, French voile), Latin vēlum (“cloth, covering”). Displaced Middle English scleire, scleyre, sleyre, slyre (“veil”) (compare German Schleier). Doublet of velum and voile.

ex.en: Is that a veiled threat?
ex.ja: それはいわゆる脅しですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 velum（覆い・帆）から。「ベール」。reveal（ベールを取る → 明らかにする）、revelation と同じ。

en: Capable of doing many things competently.
Having varied uses or many functions.

versatile.ety: From Latin versātilis (“turning easily”), from versātus, past participle of versō (“to turn, change”), frequentative of vertō (“to turn”).

ex.en: This seasoning is so versatile that you can put it on anything.
ex.ja: この調味料、万能すぎて何にでもかけてる。

en: The scientific study of humans, systematically describing the ethnographic, linguistic, archaeological, and evolutionary dimensions of hu…
The study of humanity in its relation to the divine, as in Christian anthropology.

anthropology.ety: From New Latin anthropologia, from Ancient Greek ἄνθρωπος (ánthrōpos, “human, mankind”) + -λογία (-logía). By surface analysis, anthropo- + -logy.

ex.en: This book deals with anthropology.
ex.ja: この本は人類学を扱っている。

ex.en: He is hailed as the father of modern anthropology.
ex.ja: 彼は現代人類学の父として熱烈な支持を受けている。

ex.en: He majors in social anthropology.
ex.ja: 彼は社会人類学を専攻している。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 anthrōpos（人間）+ logia（学）。「人類学」。philanthropy（人類愛）と同じ。

en: Any of the muscular- and elastic-walled blood vessels forming part of the circulation system by which blood is conveyed away from the hea…
A major transit corridor in a system of roads, rivers, or railway lines.

artery.ety: Late Middle English arterie, borrowing from Old French artaire and Latin artēria (“a windpipe; an artery”), from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓ρτηρῐ́ᾱ (ărtērĭ́ā, “windpipe; artery”).

ex.en: Lungs, heart, veins, arteries and capillaries form the cardiovascular system.
ex.ja: 肺、心臓、静脈、動脈、毛細血管により循環器系が形成されています。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 artēria（気管・動脈）から。昔は動脈が空気を運ぶと考えられた。「動脈」→「幹線道路」。

en: Any of the fast-growing grasses of the Bambusoideae subfamily, characterized by its woody, hollow, round, straight, jointed stem.
Wood of the bamboo plant as a material for building, furniture, etc.
Made of the wood of the bamboo.
To flog with a bamboo cane.
To paint (furniture, etc.) to give it the appearance of bamboo.

bamboo.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Dravidian *wē
Proto-Dravidian *mpu
Proto-Dravidian *wēmpu
Tamil வேம்பு (vēmpu)der.
▲
Proto-Dravidian *wēmpu

Malay bambubor.

Dutch bamboebor.
English bamboo
Borrowed from Dutch bamboe, from Portuguese bambu, from Malay bambu, from Kannada ಬಂಬು (bambu), variant form of ಬೇವು (bēvu). Cognate with Malayalam വേപ്പ് (vēppŭ), Tamil வேம்பு (vēmpu), Telugu వేప (vēpa), from Proto-Dravidian *wēmpu (“neem”).

ex.en: I made a table out of bamboo.
ex.ja: 竹でテーブルを作りました。

ex.en: The bamboo gave but did not break.
ex.ja: その竹はしなったが折れなかった。

ex.en: There's bamboo growing in the garden.
ex.ja: 庭に竹が生えている。

note.ja: マレー語 bambu から、オランダ語を経た語。「竹」。

en: A plant (Ocimum basilicum).
The leaves of this plant used as a herb.
To grind the edge of a tool to an acute angle.

basil.ety: Inherited from Middle English basile, from Middle French basile, from Old French basile, from Medieval Latin basilicum, from Ancient Greek βασιλικόν (basilikón, “royal”), from βασιλεύς (basileús, “king”). Doublet of basilic, basilicon, and basilicum; further related to basileus, basilean, and basileiolatry.

ex.en: I like to add basil to season my spaghetti sauce.
ex.ja: スパゲッティのソースにバジルを加えるのが好きです。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 basilikon（王の（草））から。basileus（王）。「バジル」。

en: A fruit-bearing shrub of the aggregate species Rubus fruticosus and some hybrids.
The soft fruit borne by this shrub, formed of a black (when ripe) cluster of drupelets.
To gather or forage for blackberries.

blackberry.ety:
Etymology tree
Old English blæcberġe
Middle English blakberie
English blackberry
From Middle English blakberie, blakeberie (“brambleberry”), from Old English blacu berġe, blæcberġe (attested in plural blaca berġan), equivalent to black + berry.

ex.en: I wonder where Tom found these blackberries.
ex.ja: トムはこのブラックベリー、どこで見つけたのかしら。

ex.en: I really like blackberries.
ex.ja: ブラックベリーが大好きなんだ。

ex.en: Tom has a Blackberry.
ex.ja: トムはBlackBerryを持ってるんだ。

note.ja: black（黒い）+ berry（実）。「ブラックベリー」。

en: Diameter of the bore of a firearm, typically measured between opposite lands.
The diameter of round or cylindrical body, as of a bullet, a projectile, or a column.

caliber.ety: From French calibre (“bore of a gun, size, capacity (literally, and figuratively), also weight”), from Italian calibro.

ex.en: "Situation report." "At present 4 in sight. At most probably 7. Holding small calibre arms."
ex.ja: 「状況報告を」「現在目標は目視４。最大７か。小口径火器を所有」

note.ja: アラビア語 qālib（型）から。「（銃の）口径」→ 人の器量 →「能力・質」。

en: A harmonic set of three or more notes that is heard as if sounding simultaneously.
A line segment between two points of a curve.
To write chords for.
To accord; to harmonize together.

chord.ety: Variant of cord, with spelling alteration due to Latin chorda (“cord”), ultimately from Ancient Greek χορδή (khordḗ, “string of gut, the string of a lyre”). No relation to French accord (“chord”) and its derivations. Doublet of cuerda.

ex.en: That name struck a chord.
ex.ja: その名にどこか聞き覚えがあった。

ex.en: The ukelele chords are always in her CD booklet.
ex.ja: 彼女のＣＤの歌詞カードにはいつもウクレレのコードが載っている。

note.ja: cord（ひも・弦）の変化形。ギリシャ語 khordē（弦）。「弦」→「和音」。accord（一致）と混ざった語。

en: A concessions stand.

ex.en: We solved the problem by mutual concessions.
ex.ja: お互い歩み寄って問題を解決した。

en: Of or pertaining to the body, especially the human body; bodily.
Pertaining to the body (the thorax and abdomen), as distinguished from the head, limbs and wings, etc.
A non-commissioned officer army rank with NATO code OR-4. The rank below a sergeant but above a lance corporal and private.
A non-commissioned officer rank in the police force, below a sergeant but above a private or patrolman.

corporal.ety: From Middle English corporal, corporall, corporel, corporell, from Old French corporal (French corporel), from Latin corporālis, from Latin corpus (“body”); compare corporeal.

ex.en: The trend of public opinion is against corporal punishment.
ex.ja: 世論の趨勢は体罰反対の方向である。

ex.en: Personally, I think that corporal punishment is a necessary evil.
ex.ja: 個人的には体罰は必要悪だと思っています。

ex.en: I'm firmly opposed to corporal punishment.
ex.ja: 私は体罰には断固反対です。

note.ja: 「伍長」はイタリア語 caporale（頭の者）から、capo（頭）。「肉体の」はラテン語 corpus（体）からで別語。

en: An area, open to the sky, partially or wholly surrounded by walls or buildings.

note.ja: court（中庭）+ yard（囲い地）。「中庭」。

en: The summit of a hill or mountain ridge.
A tuft, or other natural ornament, growing on an animal's head, for example the comb of a cockerel, the swelling on the head of a snake, …
Particularly with reference to waves, to reach a peak.
To reach the crest of (e.g. a hill or mountain).

crest.ety:

ex.en: Legislators in the Diet are struggling to find a solution to the problem.
ex.ja: 国会議員は問題の解決に苦慮しています。

note.ja: ラテン語 legis lator（法を持ち込む人）。lex（法）+ lator（運ぶ人）。「立法者」。legislation と同じ。

en: A crustacean of the Nephropidae family, dark green or blue-black in colour turning bright red when cooked, with a hard shell and claws, w…
A spiny lobster, also called the rock lobster, a crustacean of the Palinuridae family, pinkish red in colour, with a hard, spiny shell bu…
To fish for lobsters.
Red-colored, especially from a sunburn.

lobster.ety:
Etymology tree
Old English loppestre
Middle English loppestere
English lobster
From Middle English loppestere, lopster, from Old English loppestre, lopustre, lopystre, of uncertain origin. Some believe it to be a corruption of Latin lō̆custa (“grasshopper, locust”) + the Old English feminine agent suffix -estre. In Latin, the phrase lō̆custa marīna (literally "sea-grasshopper") signified a type of crustacean (shrimp or lobster).
Alternatively, from Old English lobbe, loppe (“spider”) + the Old English feminine agent suffix -estre, equivalent to lop + -ster.

ex.en: Lobsters belong to a class of marine animals.
ex.ja: ロブスターは海洋動物の一種に属します。

ex.en: I don't want to eat a live lobster.
ex.ja: 私は生きたままのえびは食べたくない。

ex.en: I want to eat lobster again tonight.
ex.ja: 今日の夜はまたロブスターが食べたいなあ。

note.ja: 古英語 loppestre から。ラテン語 locusta（イナゴ・エビ）と、loppe（クモ）が混ざった語。locust（イナゴ）と同じ語源。

en: A feeling of depression resulting from being alone or from having no companions.
The condition or state of being alone or having no companions.

ex.en: Life has a loneliness one cannot truly understand until reaching old age.
ex.ja: 人生には老年にならぬと解らない淋しい気持があるものだ。

ex.en: Sometimes I have feelings of being tormented by loneliness.
ex.ja: 時々、孤独感に苛まれることがあります。

ex.en: Guinea pigs can die of loneliness.
ex.ja: モルモットは孤独死しちゃうんだ。

note.ja: lonely（寂しい）+ -ness。lone は alone の短縮。「孤独」。

en: A disease spread by mosquito, in which a protozoan, Plasmodium, multiplies in blood every few days.

malaria.ety: Borrowed from Italian malaria, formed from mal- (“bad”) and aria (“air”). Introduced into English by the Scottish geologist John MacCulloch (1773–1835). Displaced native Old English unlyft (literally “bad air”).

ex.en: Malaria is a disease that mosquitoes carry.
ex.ja: マラリアは蚊が運ぶ病気です。

ex.en: Malaria is carried by mosquitoes.
ex.ja: マラリアは蚊が媒介する。

ex.en: He contracted malaria while living in the jungle.
ex.ja: 彼はジャングルに住んでいる間にマラリアにかかった。

note.ja: イタリア語 mala aria（悪い空気）から。沼地の悪い空気が原因と考えられたことから。

en: A public declaration of principles, policies, or intentions, especially that of a political party.
To issue a manifesto.

manifesto.ety: Since the mid 17th century, from Italian manifesto, from manifestare + -o, from Latin manifestō (“to make public”), from Latin manus + an uncertain second element. Doublet of manifest.

note.ja: イタリア語 manifesto（明らかにすること）から。manifest と同じ。「宣言・マニフェスト」。

en: A labyrinth; a puzzle consisting of a complicated network of paths or passages, the aim of which is to find one's way through.
Something made up of many confused or conflicting elements; a tangle.

maze.ety: From Middle English mase, from Middle English masen (“to perplex, bewilder”); or perhaps from Old English *mæs (“delusion, bewilderment”); akin to Old English āmasian (“to perplex, confound”), Icelandic masa (“to chatter”). More at amaze.

ex.en: This maze is very hard to get out of.
ex.ja: この迷路は抜け出すのがとても難しい。

ex.en: Yesterday we went into a huge maze.
ex.ja: 昨日大きな迷路に入りました。

ex.en: The boy could not find his way out of the maze.
ex.ja: 少年は迷路から抜け出せなかった。

note.ja: amaze（呆然とさせる）と同じ語。「頭を混乱させるもの」→「迷路」。

en: A residence for monks or others who have taken religious vows.

monastery.ety: From Middle English monasterie, from Old French monastere, from Medieval Latin monastērium (“monastery”), from Ancient Greek μοναστήριον (monastḗrion, “hermitage, monastery”), from μοναστήριος (monastḗrios, “alone, made alone”) + -ιον (-ion, “-ium”, suffix forming place names), from μονάζω (monázō, “to be alone”), from μόνος (mónos, “alone”) + -άζω (-ázō, verb-forming suffix). Doublet of minster.

ex.en: Monks used to play tennis in monasteries.
ex.ja: 当時は修道僧達が修道院でよくテニスをしていた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 monastērion から。monazein（ひとりで暮らす）、monos。「修道院」。monk と同じ。

en: Any alteration or change.
Any heritable change of the base-pair sequence of genetic material.

mutation.ety: Late 14th century as Middle English mutacioun, from Latin mūtātiō, both directly and via Old French mutacion.

ex.en: Without the random mutation of genes there would be no evolution.
ex.ja: 遺伝子の突然変異がなければ、進化は起こりえない。

ex.en: White strawberries were born of a mutation during selective breeding.
ex.ja: 白いちごは、品種改良中の突然変異によって生まれました。

note.ja: mut（変える）+ ation。変わること →「突然変異・変化」。

en: In a narrow manner; without flexibility or latitude.
Closely; by a narrow margin.

narrowly.ety: From Middle English narowly, equivalent to narrow + -ly.

ex.en: The federal budget was narrowly approved by Congress.
ex.ja: 連邦予算はかろうじて議会の承認を得た。

ex.en: The budget was narrowly approved by Congress.
ex.ja: 予算はかろうじて議会の承認を得た。

ex.en: I narrowly escaped being hit by a car.
ex.ja: かろうじて車に当てられずにすんだ。

note.ja: narrow（狭い）+ -ly。「狭く」→ ぎりぎりで →「かろうじて」。

en: The state of being negligent.
The tort whereby a duty of reasonable care was breached, causing damage: any conduct short of intentional or reckless action that falls b…

negligence.ety: From Middle English necligence, negligence, from Old French negligence, from Latin neglegentia.

ex.en: This failure was brought about by your own negligence.
ex.ja: この失敗は、君自身の怠慢から起こったものだ。

ex.en: The accident happened because of the driver's negligence.
ex.ja: その事故は運転手の不注意から起きた。

ex.en: The accident was due to the negligence of the caretaker.
ex.ja: その事故の責任は管理人の怠慢にある。

note.ja: neglect（怠る）と同じ語源。ラテン語 neglegere ＝ neg（否定）+ legere（選ぶ・拾う）。「拾わない」→「怠慢・過失」。

Of, or relating to optics or optical instruments.
A lens or other part of an optical instrument that interacts with light.
A measuring device with a small window, attached to an upside-down bottle, used to dispense alcoholic drinks in a bar.

ex.en: His study of optics led him to the invention of the magnifying glass.
ex.ja: 光学の研究で彼は拡大鏡の発明をした。

ex.ja: その二人の兄弟はうり二つである。

ex.ja: グリンピース買ってきて。冷凍のやつね。

en: The way a person holds and positions their body.
A situation or condition.
To put one's body into a posture or series of postures, especially hoping that one will be noticed and admired.
To pretend to have an opinion or a conviction.

posture.ety: Borrowed from Middle French posture, from Italian postura, from Latin positūra (“position, situation”). Doublet of positura.

ex.en: Use good posture while eating.
ex.ja: 犬食いはみっともないよね。

ex.en: He likes to posture as an intellectual.
ex.ja: 彼は知識人ぶるのが好きだ。

ex.ja: オープン戦だけ絶好調だった。

note.ja: pre（前の）+ season（シーズン）。「シーズン前」。

en: To renew or revitalize.
To become fresh again; to be revitalized.
The periodic energizing required to maintain the contents of computer memory, the display luminance of a computer screen, etc.
The update of a display (in a web browser or similar software) to show the latest version of the data.

refresh.ety: From Middle English refreshen, refreschen, refrisschen, from Old French refrescher (“to refresh”) (modern French rafraîchir), equivalent to re- + fresh.

ex.ja: お茶を一杯飲んで彼は元気が出た。

ex.en: She refreshed her memory with the photo.
ex.ja: 彼女はその写真を見ると記憶がよみがえってきた。

ex.en: A glass of orange juice refreshed me.
ex.ja: オレンジジュースを飲んだら気分がさわやかになった。

en: The quality of being resonant.
A resonant sound, echo, or reverberation, such as that produced by blowing over the top of a bottle.

resonance.ety: From Old French resonance (French résonance), from Latin resonantia (“echo”), from resonō (“to resound”).

ex.en: By using four types of metal, specific frequency resonance is suppressed.
ex.ja: 四種類の金属を使うことで特定の共振を抑えます。

note.ja: resonate（共鳴する）+ -ance。re（再び）+ sonare（鳴る）。「鳴り返すこと」→「共鳴・反響」。sound、sonic と同じ son。

en: A literary device of writing or art which principally ridicules its subject often as an intended means of provoking or preventing change …
A satirical work.

satire.ety: From Middle French satire, from Old French, from Latin satira, from earlier satura, from lanx satura (“full dish”), from feminine of satur. ex.ja: その賞賛は皮肉の変装したものであることに彼は気がつかなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 satura（いろいろ盛った皿・ごった煮）から。「ごった煮の詩」→「風刺」。

Food from any aquatic source, including not only salt water but also fresh water.

en: A swift, broad cutting stroke, especially one made with an edged weapon or whip.
A wide striking motion made with an implement such as a cricket bat, hockey stick, or lacrosse stick.
To cut with a swift broad stroke of an edged weapon.
To produce a similar wound with a savage strike of a whip.
Used to note the sound or action of a slash.
Used to connect two or more identities in a list.
Used to list alternatives.

slash.ety:
Late Middle English, originally a verb of uncertain etymology. Perhaps of imitative origin, or possibly from Old French esclachier (“to break in pieces”), a variant of esclater, which is likely a Germanic borrowing, from Frankish *slaitan (“to slit, tear”).
Used in the Wycliffe Bible as slascht (see 1 Kings 5:18) but otherwise unattested until 16th century. Conjunctive use from various applications of the punctuation mark ⟨/⟩. See also slash fiction.

ex.en: The Federal Reserve slashed interest rates.
ex.ja: 米国連邦準備銀行は金利を引き下げました。

ex.en: Japanese corporations are slashing their capital spending programs.
ex.ja: 日本の企業はいま投資支出計画を削減している。

note.ja: 中英語 slaschen から。擬音的な語。「切りつける」→ 大胆に削る →「大幅に削減する」、切り傷のような線 →「斜線」。

To serve (someone) spaghetti (noun noun 1 sense 1).
To cause (someone or something) to become, or appear to become, longer and thinner; to stretch.

ex.ja: 私、パスタ料理がすごく得意なの。

ex.en: You have some spaghetti sauce on your face.
ex.ja: 顔にスパゲッティーのソースがついているよ。

ex.en: At this restaurant, you eat spaghetti with chopsticks.
ex.ja: このお店ではスパゲッティをお箸でいただくんです。

en: Proceeding with or characterized by high speed; rapid.
To process in a faster than normal, accelerated way.
To apply the speedy rule in an online community (often the deletion rule); to speedy delete.

speedy.ety: From Middle English spedy, spedi, from Old English spēdiġ (“having good speed, lucky, prosperous; having means, wealthy, opulent, rich in material wealth; rich in, abounding in, abundant, plenteous, copious; powerful”), from Proto-West Germanic *spōdīg (“successful, hurried”), equivalent to speed + -y. Cognate with Scots speedy (“speedy”), West Frisian spoedich (“speedily, quickly, soon”), Dutch spoedig (“speedy, swift, rapid, quick”), Low German spoodig, spödig (“hasty, fast, swift, quick”), German sputig, spudig (“industrious, speedy”).

ex.en: I wish your father a speedy recovery.
ex.ja: お父さんが早く良くなりますように。

ex.en: The doctor's quick arrival brought about her very speedy recovery.
ex.ja: 医者がすぐ来てくれたので、彼女は早く回復した。

ex.en: The doctor's careful examination of the patient brought about his speedy recovery.
ex.ja: 医者が患者を丹念に診察したおかげで、患者はどんどんよくなった。

note.ja: speed（速さ）+ -y。「迅速な」。

en: A point of view; a perspective.

standpoint.ety: From stand + point, a calque of German Standpunkt. Similar constructions used in other languages, such as Japanese 立場 (tachiba, literally “standing place”).

ex.ja: いろいろな観点からその問題を検討できる。

ex.en: From the standpoint of the law, he is free.
ex.ja: 法律の観点からすると、彼は自由だ。

ex.en: From this standpoint history can be divided into two main epochs.
ex.ja: この見地から歴史は２つの主要な時期に分けられる。

note.ja: stand（立つ）+ point（地点）。ドイツ語 Standpunkt のなぞり。「立つ位置」→「観点・立場」。

en: The act of swaying; a swaying motion; a swing or sweep of a weapon.
A rocking or swinging motion.
To move or swing from side to side; or backward and forward; to rock.
To move or wield with the hand; to swing; to wield.

sway.ety:

The noun derived from the verb.

ex.en: Tall buildings may sway in a strong wind.
ex.ja: 強風が吹けば高層ビルは揺れるだろう。

ex.en: He has never swayed from his duty.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の本分を踏み外したことがない。

ex.en: The ship swayed in the strong wind.
ex.ja: 船は強い風を受けて揺れた。

note.ja: 北欧語 sveigja（曲げる）から。「揺れる・揺さぶる」→「左右する」。

en: To end something, especially when left in an incomplete state.
To conclude.
Terminated; limited; bounded; ended.
Having a definite and clear limit or boundary; having a determinate size, shape or magnitude.

terminate.ety: From Middle English terminaten (“to bring to an end; to adjudicate; to end, stop; to border, confine, contain”) from terminat(e) (“bounded”, also used as the past participle of terminaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), borrowed from Latin terminātus, perfect passive participle of terminō (“to set bounds to, bound, limit, end, close, terminate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from terminus (“a bound, limit, end”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix); see term, terminus. ex.en: The Tokaido line terminates at Tokyo.
ex.ja: 東海道線は東京が終点だ。

note.ja: termin（境界・終わり）+ ate。終わりにする →「終わらせる・解雇する」。

en: An unoccupied position or job.
An available room in a hotel; guest house, etc.

en: To resist or endure (something) successfully.
To oppose (something) forcefully.

ex.ja: 私の家は地震に堪えるように設計されている。

ex.ja: ロボットなら危険な状態になっても切り抜けられる。

Land covered with woody vegetation.
A low-density forest.

ex.ja: 走者がリレーでバトンを渡さなければなりません。

The termination of a friendship or a romantic relationship.

ex.ja: 噛みつくといけないのでそのブルドッグに近寄るな。

Of a light brown color like that of a camel.

ex.ja: その砂漠で私たちはラクダを使わなかった。

ex.ja: この国では、ラクダはなくてはならない。

The process of checking out items at a supermarket or library.

To break down (language, etc.) into conceptual pieces of manageable size.

ex.ja: 巨大な肉の塊が当たった。

ex.ja: 昨夜、私はもどしてしまった。

ex.ja: 彼は級友と仲が良い。

ex.ja: ココアでもどうですか？

This word has probably survived as long as it has due to its coincidental phonetic resemblance to the unrelated word English cave. Also unrelated to Spanish cueva, which itself is a cognate of cave.

en: To fear greatly.
To anticipate with fear.
Great fear in view of impending evil; fearful apprehension of danger; anticipatory terror.
Reverential or respectful fear; awe.
Terrible; greatly feared; dreaded.

dread.ety:
From Middle English dreden, from Old English drǣdan (“to fear, dread”), aphetic form of ondrǣdan (“to fear, dread”), from Proto-West Germanic *andarādan, equivalent to Old English and- + rǣdan (whence read); corresponding to an aphesis of earlier adread.
Akin to Old Saxon antdrādan, andrādan (“to fear, dread”), Old High German intrātan (“to fear”), Middle High German entrāten (“to fear, dread, frighten”).

ex.ja: 彼は父親を絶えず恐れている。

en: To confer knighthood; the conclusion of the ceremony was marked by a tap on the shoulder with a sword, the accolade.
To name, to entitle, to call.
A poorly executed shot.

dub.ety:
From Middle English dubben, from Old English dubbian (“to knight by striking with a sword, dub”) from Old French adober (“to equip with arms; adorn”) (also 11th century, Modern French adouber), both from Proto-West Germanic *dubbōn, from Proto-Germanic *dub- (“to hit, strike”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewbʰ- (“plug, peg, wedge”).
Cognate with Icelandic dubba (in dubba til riddara). Compare also drub for an English reflex of the Germanic word.

ex.en: Ah, if you can dub it, can I ask for a copy as well?

note.ja: 「吹き替える」は double（二重にする）の短縮。「〜と呼ぶ」は古英語 dubbian（騎士に叙する）からで別語。

To feint.

ex.en: The corporation set up a dummy company.

en: The collective people of a country, state, or electoral district who are entitled to vote.
The office, or area of dominion, of an Elector (“a German prince entitled to elect the emperor of the Holy Roman Empire”); an electorship.

electorate.ety: From elector (“person eligible to vote in an election; German prince entitled to elect the emperor of the Holy Roman Empire”) + -ate (forms nouns denoting a rank or office, the concrete charge of it).

note.ja: elector（選挙人）+ -ate。e（外へ）+ legere（選ぶ）。「有権者（全体）」。elect と同じ。

en: The result of having been worn away or eroded, as by a glacier on rock or the sea on a cliff face.
The changing of a surface by mechanical action, friction, thermal expansion contraction, or impact.

erosion.ety:
From Middle French erosion, from Latin ērōsiō (“eating away”), derived from ērōdō.
The first known occurrence in English was in the 1541 translation by Robert Copland of Guy de Chauliac's medical text The Questyonary of Cyrurygens. Copland used erosion to describe how ulcers developed in the mouth. By 1774 erosion was used outside medical subjects. Oliver Goldsmith employed the term in the more contemporary geological context, in his book Natural History, with the quote
: "Bounds are thus put to the erosion of the earth by water."

ex.en: If the trees on that hill are cut down, you'll see erosion pretty quickly.
ex.ja: もしあの丘の木々が切り倒されたら、急速に浸食を見ることになるだろう。

note.ja: erode（浸食する）+ -sion。e（外へ）+ rodere（かじる）。「かじり取られること」→「浸食」。rodent（げっ歯類）と同じ。

Origin uncertain, first recorded in the mid 16th century, probably related to Latin flagrō (“to burn”). Norwegian flara (“to blaze; to flaunt in gaudy attire”) has a similar meaning, but the English word predates it. The noun is derived from the verb.

pillar.ety: From Middle English piler, from Old French pilier, from Medieval Latin or Vulgar Latin *pilāre (“a pillar”), from Latin pila (“a pillar, pier, mole”). Displaced native Old English sweor (“pillar, column”) and Old English stapol.

ex.en: There was a knife stuck in the pillar.
ex.ja: 柱にナイフが突き刺さっていた。

ex.en: These pillars are made of stone.
ex.ja: これは石柱である。

ex.en: These pillars support the stage.
ex.ja: これらの柱が舞台を支えています。

note.ja: ラテン語 pila（柱）から。「柱」→ 組織を支える人 →「中心人物」。pile（杭）と同系。

en: Seemingly or apparently valid, likely, or acceptable; conceivably true or likely.
Obtaining approbation; specifically pleasing; apparently right; specious.

plausible.ety: From Latin plausibilis (“deserving applause, praiseworthy, acceptable, pleasing”), from the participle stem of plaudere (“to applaud”).

ex.en: Your explanation sounds plausible, but it just doesn't hold water.
ex.ja: 君の説明はもっともらしいが、筋がちっとも通ってない。

ex.en: You're spitting out plausible lies.
ex.ja: もっともらしい嘘をつきやがって。

ex.en: A more plausible proposal is the one Leech presented in conjunction with Emmet's theory.
ex.ja: リーチがエメット理論との関連で提供した提案のほうがより妥当なものである。

note.ja: ラテン語 plaudere（拍手する）から。拍手に値しそうな →「もっともらしい・妥当な」。applause（拍手）と同じ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 poly（多くの）+ meros（部分）。「多くの部分がつながったもの」→「重合体」。

The amount of water precipitated in any form.

en: A period of 40 days, particularly
The 40-day period during which a widow is entitled to remain in her deceased husband's home while any dower is collected and returned.
To place into isolation to prevent the spread of any contagious disease.
To enter or stay in quarantine, particularly to self-quarantine to avoid an epidemic disease.

quarantine.ety:
From Medieval Latin quarentena and quarentīna (“40-day period, Lent”) via Middle English quarentine, Norman quarenteine, French quarenteine, and Italian quarantina, via proposed Late Latin *quaranta + -ēna (forming distributive adjectives), from Latin quadrāgintā (“four tens, 40”).
In reference to French politics, calque of French quarantaine after edicts of Louis IX. In reference to a severance of political relations, popularized by the Roosevelt administration's 1937 approach to the Axis powers and the later Kennedy administration's 1962 approach to Cuba during the missile crisis.

ex.en: People returning from Spain are required to self-quarantine for 14 days.
ex.ja: スペインから帰国する人全員に14日間の自主隔離を義務付けた。

ex.en: The hospital quarantined the infected patients to avoid cross infection.
ex.ja: 病院は院内感染を防ぐため、感染患者を隔離した。

note.ja: イタリア語 quaranta giorni（40日）から。ペスト流行時、船を40日間停泊させて隔離したことから。

en: A question, an inquiry (US), an enquiry (UK).
A question mark.
To ask a question.
To ask, inquire.

query.ety: An anglicisation of quere, an obsolete variant form of Latin quaere, second-person singular present active imperative of quaerō (“seek, look for; ask”); perhaps suffixed with -y (“abstract noun”). Cognate with French quérir, Italian chiedere, Portuguese querer, Romanian cere, and Spanish querer. Compare question.

ex.en: The saleswoman queried as she wrapped the gloves.
ex.ja: 美人店員は手袋を袋に包みながら尋ねた。

note.ja: ラテン語 quaere（尋ねよ）から。quer（求める・尋ねる）+ y。→「質問・問い合わせ・疑問」。

en: Something that restrains, ties, fastens or secures.
Control or caution; reserve.

restraint.ety: From Middle English restreynte, from Old French restreinte; more at restrain.

ex.en: She was angry, but she spoke with restraint.
ex.ja: 彼女は怒っていたが、それをおさえて話をした。

ex.en: He refused to exercise self-restraint.
ex.ja: 彼は自粛の波に乗らなかった。

ex.en: Institutionally, a major restraint is the copyright problem.
ex.ja: 制度的に大きな枷となるのは、著作権の問題である。

en: A chasm or fissure.
A lack of cohesion; a state of conflict, incompatibility, or emotional distance.
To form a rift; to split open.
To cleave; to rive; to split.

rift.ety: From Middle English rift, of North Germanic origin; akin to Danish rift, Norwegian Bokmål rift (“breach”), Old Norse rífa (“to tear”). More at rive.

note.ja: 北欧語 ript（裂け目）から。rive（裂く）と同系。「亀裂・不和」。

ex.ja: 彼はセールスマンをして生計をたてている。

ex.ja: 彼女はセールスマンにだまされた。

note.ja: sale（販売）+ s + man。「販売員」。

en: A brilliant red colour sometimes tinged with orange.
Cloth of a scarlet color.
Of a bright red colour.
Sinful or whorish.
To dye or tinge (something) with scarlet.

scarlet.ety: From Middle English scarlet, scarlat, borrowed from Old French escarlate (“a type of cloth”), from Medieval Latin scarlātum (“scarlet cloth”), of uncertain origin. en: A pipe or channel, or system of pipes or channels, used to remove human waste and to provide drainage.
To provide (a place) with a system of sewers.

sewer.ety: From Middle English sewer, seuer, from Anglo-Norman sewere (“water-course”), from Old French sewiere (“overflow channel for a fishpond”), from Vulgar Latin *exaquāria (“drain for carrying water off”), from Latin ex (“out of, from”) + aquāria (“of or pertaining to waters”) or from a root *exaquāre.

en: A distinct flavor, especially if slight.
A slight trace of something; a smattering.
To get the flavor of.
To have a particular taste; used with of.
As if with a smack or slap; smartly; sharply.

smack.ety:
The noun is from Middle English smac, smak, smacke, from Old English smæc, smæċċ (“taste, smatch”), from Proto-West Germanic *smakku, from Proto-Germanic *smakkuz (“a taste”), from Proto-Indo-European *smegʰ-, *smeg- (“to taste”). ex.en: She smacked him across the face.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼の顔に平手打ちを食わせた。

ex.en: I'll smack the living daylights out of you!
ex.ja: ぶっ飛ばしてやる！

ex.en: I'll give you a smack in the hand if you eat with your fingers.
ex.ja: つまみ食いしたら、おててぺっちんするからね。

note.ja: 「ぴしゃりと打つ」は擬音語。「味がする（smack of）」は古英語 smæc（味）からで別語。

en: Of or pertaining to the southwest.

southwestern.ety: From Middle English southwesterne, from Old English sūþwesterne, equivalent to south + western.

note.ja: south + west + -ern。「南西の」。

en: A person who acts as the voice of another person or a group of people.

spokesperson.ety: From spoke (“past participle of speak”) + -s- + person.

note.ja: spokesman を性別に中立にした語。「報道官」。

en: The act of going stealthily.
Hunting for game by moving silently and stealthily or by waiting in ambush.

stalking.ety: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

note.ja: stalk（忍び寄る）+ -ing。stalk は steal（盗む・こっそり動く）と同系。「ストーカー行為」。

en: Designed or constructed in a standard manner or according to an official standard.
A single pass of a needle in sewing; the loop or turn of the thread thus made.
A single pass of a surgical suture (to sew the edges of a wound together)
To form stitches in; especially, to sew in such a manner as to show on the surface a continuous line of stitches.
To sew, or unite or attach by stitches.

stitch.ety:
From Middle English stiche, from Old English stiċe (“a prick, puncture, stab, thrust with a pointed implement, pricking sensation, stitch, pain in the side, sting”), from Proto-West Germanic *stiki, from Proto-Germanic *stikiz (“prick, piercing, stitch”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teyg- (“to stab, pierce”).
Cognate with Dutch steek (“prick, stitch”), German Stich (“a prick, piercing, stitch”), Old English stician (“to stick, stab, pierce, prick”). More at stick. Via PIE cognate with Czech steh, Polish ścieg, Russian стежо́к (stežók).

ex.en: He didn't do a stitch of work.
ex.ja: 彼は少しも仕事をしなかった。

ex.en: Your stitches will be removed in a few days.
ex.ja: 抜糸は数日後になります。

ex.en: You're going to need a few stitches.
ex.ja: 何針か、縫わないといけないですね。

note.ja: 古英語 stice（刺すこと）から。stick（刺す）と同系。「縫い目・ひと針」。A stitch in time saves nine.（早めの一針は九針の手間を省く）。

The substance lining the bottom edge of an enclosure.
Having very slight furrows.

ja: スルタン（イスラム国家の君主）

ex.en: Once the Sultan ruled over what today is Turkey.
ex.ja: かつてサルタンが今日のトルコを統治していた。

note.ja: アラビア語 sulṭān（権力・支配者）から。「スルタン」。

Power over all others.

To cause to become bigger.
The act of swelling; increase in size.
A bulge or protuberance.
Very well.

swell.ety:
From Middle English swellen, from Old English swellan (“to swell”), from Proto-West Germanic *swellan, from Proto-Germanic *swellaną (“to swell”), of unknown origin.

ex.en: My hands became swollen up while taking a long bath.
ex.ja: 長くお風呂に入っていたら手がふやけてしまった。

ex.ja: 手足がむくんでいます。

ex.ja: 舌が腫れて、味覚がない！

en: The act of asserting; positive declaration or averment.
Something which is asserted; a declaration; a statement asserted.

assertion.ety: From Middle English assercioun, from Latin assertiō. By surface analysis, assert + -ion.

ex.en: Nobody will believe his assertion that he is innocent.
ex.ja: 無実だという彼の主張は誰も信じないだろう。

ex.en: It is important to note that his assertion is groundless.
ex.ja: 彼の主張には根拠がないことに注意することが重要である。

en: The study of the physical universe beyond the Earth's atmosphere, including the process of mapping locations and properties of the matter…

astronomy.ety: From Middle English astronomie, astronemy, from Old French astronomie, equivalent to astro- + -nomy. Displaced native Old English tungolcræft.

ex.en: It seems that he is interested in astronomy.
ex.ja: 彼は天文学に興味があるようだ。

ex.en: What really interests me a lot is astronomy.
ex.ja: 私がとても興味を抱いているのは天文学だ。

ex.en: Astronomy is by no means a new science.
ex.ja: 天文学は決して新しい科学ではない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 astron（星）+ nomos（法則）。「星の法則」→「天文学」。astrology（星の学 → 占星術）と区別。

en: The space, often unfinished and with sloped walls, directly below the roof in the uppermost part of a house or other building, generally …
A storey or a parapet above the cornice of a classical façade, often decorated.

attic.ety: From the practice of decorating the top storey of building facades in the Attic architectural style. From French attique, from Latin atticus, from Ancient Greek Ἀττικός (Attikós).

ex.en: Is it still up in the attic?
ex.ja: それって、まだ屋根裏部屋にあるの？

ex.en: Who knows what we'll find up in the attic?
ex.ja: 屋根裏部屋で何が見つかるかなんてわからないよ。

ex.en: Tom found a box in the attic.
ex.ja: トムは屋根裏部屋で、箱を一つ見つけた。

note.ja: 古代ギリシャのアッティカ（Attica）式の柱飾りから。最上階の装飾部分 →「屋根裏部屋」。

A piece of equipment used to transmit audio and/or video content, or messages, to be received by radios or televisions, over the internet…

ex.en: NHK is a public broadcaster.
ex.ja: ＮＨＫは公共放送です。

en: Such a store of physical supplies, placed by humans or other animals for practical reasons.
A fast temporary storage where recently or frequently used information is stored to avoid having to reload it from a slower storage medium.
To place in a cache.
To store data in a cache.

cache.ety: From French cache (as used by French Canadian trappers to mean “hiding place for stores”), from the verb cacher (“to hide”).

note.ja: フランス語 cacher（隠す）から。「隠し場所」→ コンピューターのデータの一時保存場所 →「キャッシュ」。
